questions.prompt: Define a scalar quantity.
questions.answer: A quantity with magnitude (size) only.

questions.prompt: Define a vector quantity.
questions.answer: A quantity with both magnitude and direction.

questions.prompt: Name one scalar quantity and one vector quantity.
questions.answer: Scalar: e.g. speed, energy, mass, distance. Vector: e.g. force, velocity, displacement, weight.

questions.prompt: State how a vector quantity can be represented.
questions.answer: By an arrow: the length shows the magnitude and the direction of the arrow shows the direction.

questions.prompt: State the difference between contact and non-contact forces.
questions.answer: Contact forces act when objects are physically touching; non-contact forces act when objects are physically separated.

questions.prompt: Name one non-contact force.
questions.answer: Gravitational, electrostatic or magnetic force.

questions.prompt: Name one contact force.
questions.answer: Friction, air resistance, tension or the normal contact force.

questions.prompt: Define a force.
questions.answer: A push or pull that acts on an object due to the interaction with another object.

questions.prompt: State whether force is a scalar or a vector quantity.
questions.answer: Vector.

questions.prompt: State the unit of weight.
questions.answer: The newton (N).

questions.prompt: State the instrument used to measure weight.
questions.answer: A calibrated spring balance (newtonmeter).

questions.prompt: Define weight.
questions.answer: The force acting on an object due to gravity.

questions.prompt: State the point at which the weight of an object may be considered to act.
questions.answer: The centre of mass.

questions.prompt: State how the weight of an object relates to its mass.
questions.answer: They are directly proportional.

questions.prompt: Define resultant force.
questions.answer: A single force that has the same effect as all the original forces acting together.

questions.prompt: Calculate the resultant of a 5 N force and a 3 N force acting in a straight line in opposite directions.
questions.answer: 2 N, in the direction of the 5 N force.

questions.prompt: State the resultant force on an object acted on by balanced forces.
questions.answer: Zero.

questions.prompt: Define one joule of work.
questions.answer: The work done when a force of one newton causes a displacement of one metre (1 J = 1 N m).

questions.prompt: State what happens to the temperature of an object when work is done against friction.
questions.answer: It increases, as energy is transferred to the thermal energy store.

questions.prompt: State when a force does work on an object.
questions.answer: When the force causes a displacement of the object (moves it through a distance).

questions.prompt: State the condition under which force is proportional to extension.
questions.answer: The limit of proportionality is not exceeded.

questions.prompt: Describe the difference between elastic and inelastic deformation.
questions.answer: Elastic: the object returns to its original shape when the force is removed. Inelastic: the object is permanently deformed.

questions.prompt: Describe the difference between a linear and a non-linear relationship between force and extension.
questions.answer: Linear: extension is directly proportional to force (a straight line through the origin). Non-linear: extension is not proportional to force (a curve).

questions.prompt: State the unit of moment.
questions.answer: The newton metre (N m).

questions.prompt: State the condition for an object to be balanced about a pivot.
questions.answer: The total clockwise moment equals the total anticlockwise moment.

questions.prompt: Define the moment of a force.
questions.answer: The turning effect of a force.

questions.prompt: State what the distance in the equation for the moment of a force is measured between.
questions.answer: The perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force.

questions.prompt: State the unit of pressure.
questions.answer: The pascal (Pa).

questions.prompt: State the direction of the force a fluid exerts on a surface.
questions.answer: Normal to (at right angles to) the surface.

questions.prompt: Define a fluid.
questions.answer: A liquid or a gas.

title: Pressure at depth in a liquid and upthrust

questions.prompt: State what affects the pressure at a point in a liquid, other than the depth.
questions.answer: The density of the liquid.

questions.prompt: State what upthrust is.
questions.answer: The resultant upward force on a submerged object, caused by the greater pressure on its bottom surface than on its top surface.

questions.prompt: State how atmospheric pressure changes with increasing height above the ground.
questions.answer: It decreases.

questions.prompt: State what causes atmospheric pressure.
questions.answer: Air molecules colliding with a surface.

questions.prompt: State how the density of the atmosphere changes with altitude.
questions.answer: It decreases; the air gets less dense as altitude increases.

questions.prompt: Define displacement.
questions.answer: The distance moved in a straight line from the start point to the finish point, together with the direction (a vector).

questions.prompt: State whether speed is a scalar or a vector quantity.
questions.answer: Scalar.

questions.prompt: State the typical walking speed.
questions.answer: About 1.5 m/s.

questions.prompt: Define distance.
questions.answer: How far an object moves (a scalar quantity: it does not involve direction).

questions.prompt: State the typical running speed of a person.
questions.answer: About 3 m/s.

questions.prompt: State the typical cycling speed of a person.
questions.answer: About 6 m/s.

questions.prompt: Calculate the distance travelled by an object moving at 15 m/s for 10 s.
State a typical value for the speed of sound in air.
questions.answer: About 330 m/s.

questions.prompt: Define velocity.
questions.answer: Speed in a given direction (a vector quantity).

questions.prompt: State what the gradient of a distance-time graph represents.
questions.answer: Speed.

questions.prompt: State what a horizontal line on a distance-time graph represents.
questions.answer: The object is stationary.

questions.prompt: State the unit of acceleration.
questions.answer: Metres per second squared (m/s²).

questions.prompt: State what the gradient of a velocity-time graph represents.
questions.answer: Acceleration.

questions.prompt: Define acceleration.
questions.answer: The rate of change of velocity (change in velocity ÷ time taken).

questions.prompt: Define deceleration.
questions.answer: The acceleration of an object that is slowing down.

title: Equations of motion for uniform acceleration

questions.prompt: State what the area under a velocity-time graph represents.
questions.answer: Distance travelled (or displacement).

questions.prompt: State the approximate acceleration of a freely falling object near the Earth's surface.
questions.answer: About 9.8 m/s².

questions.prompt: Define terminal velocity.
questions.answer: The constant velocity reached by an object falling through a fluid when the resultant force on it is zero.

questions.prompt: State why an object falling through a fluid initially accelerates.
questions.answer: The force of gravity is greater than the resistive (drag) force.

questions.prompt: State the resultant force on an object moving at terminal velocity.
questions.answer: Zero.

questions.prompt: State Newton's First Law of motion.
questions.answer: An object remains at rest, or continues at a constant velocity, unless acted on by a resultant force.

questions.prompt: Calculate the resultant force needed to accelerate a 2 kg object at 3 m/s².
State how the acceleration of an object changes when its mass is doubled and the resultant force is kept constant.
questions.answer: It halves.

questions.prompt: Define inertial mass.
questions.answer: The ratio of force over acceleration; a measure of how difficult it is to change the velocity of an object.

questions.prompt: Calculate the resultant force needed to accelerate a 1200 kg car at 2 m/s².
State Newton's Second Law of motion.
questions.answer: The acceleration of an object is proportional to the resultant force acting on it, and inversely proportional to its mass.

questions.prompt: State Newton's Third Law.
questions.answer: When two objects interact, the forces they exert on each other are equal and opposite.

questions.prompt: Define inertia.
questions.answer: The tendency of an object to continue in its state of rest or of uniform motion.

questions.prompt: State how the two forces in an interaction pair compare in size and direction.
questions.answer: They are equal in size and opposite in direction, and act on different objects.

questions.prompt: State what the stopping distance of a vehicle is made up of.
questions.answer: Thinking distance plus braking distance.

questions.prompt: Define thinking distance.
questions.answer: The distance the vehicle travels during the driver's reaction time.

questions.prompt: State how the stopping distance of a vehicle changes as its speed increases, for a given braking force.
questions.answer: It increases.

questions.prompt: Define braking distance.
questions.answer: The distance a vehicle travels under the braking force.

questions.prompt: Define stopping distance.
questions.answer: The sum of the distance travelled during the driver’s reaction time (thinking distance) and the distance travelled under the braking force (braking distance).

questions.prompt: State the typical range of human reaction times.
questions.answer: About 0.2 s to 0.9 s.

questions.prompt: Name two factors that can affect a driver's reaction time.
questions.answer: Tiredness, drugs, alcohol or distractions (any two).

questions.prompt: Describe a simple method for measuring human reaction time.
questions.answer: E.g. the ruler drop test: a ruler is dropped and the distance it falls before it is caught is used to calculate the reaction time.

questions.prompt: Name two adverse road conditions that increase braking distance.
questions.answer: Wet or icy roads.

questions.prompt: State how worn brakes or tyres affect braking distance.
questions.answer: They increase the braking distance.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the temperature of a vehicle's brakes when they are applied.
questions.answer: It increases, because work done by friction heats the brakes.

questions.prompt: State the unit of momentum.
questions.answer: kg m/s (kilogram metre per second).

questions.prompt: Calculate the momentum of a 1000 kg car travelling at 20 m/s.
Define momentum.
questions.answer: The product of an object’s mass and its velocity (p = mv); a property of moving objects.

questions.prompt: State the principle of conservation of momentum.
questions.answer: In a closed system, the total momentum before an event equals the total momentum after the event.

questions.prompt: State the total momentum of a system before a collision if all the objects are stationary.
questions.answer: Zero.

questions.prompt: State what must be true of a system for its momentum to be conserved.
questions.answer: No external resultant force acts on it (it is a closed system).

questions.prompt: Define a closed system.
questions.answer: A system in which no external forces act and nothing is transferred in or out, so its total energy and momentum stay constant.

questions.prompt: State what force is equal to, in words.
questions.answer: The rate of change of momentum.

questions.prompt: Explain how a cushioned surface or air bag reduces the force on a person in a collision.
questions.answer: It increases the time over which the momentum changes, so the rate of change of momentum, and therefore the force, is reduced.
